questions.chapter_title: Alpha Carbon Chemistry: Enols and Enolates
questions.topic: Keto-Enol Tautomerism Acid vs Base Mechanism
questions.question: What is the difference in intermediate charge state between acid-catalyzed and base-catalyzed keto-enol tautomerism?

options.label: A
options.text: Base catalysis proceeds with retention; acid catalysis with inversion.

options.label: B
options.text: There is no intermediate in either pathway.

options.label: C
options.text: Acid catalysis forms a radical; base catalysis forms an anion.

options.label: D
options.text: Acid catalysis proceeds via a positively charged oxocarbenium intermediate, whereas base catalysis proceeds via a negatively charged resonance-stabilized enolate intermediate.

questions.correct_answer: Acid catalysis proceeds via a positively charged oxocarbenium intermediate, whereas base catalysis proceeds via a negatively charged resonance-stabilized enolate intermediate.
questions.explanation: Acid mechanisms feature protonation first (cationic intermediates); base mechanisms feature deprotonation first (anionic enolate intermediates).

questions.chapter_title: Alpha Carbon Chemistry: Enols and Enolates
questions.question: Why does lithium diisopropylamide (LDA) at -78°C selectively abstract the less hindered α-proton of 2-methylcyclohexanone?

options.label: A
options.text: The less substituted enolate is thermodynamically more stable.

options.label: B
options.text: LDA is a weak base that equilibrates to the thermodynamic product.

options.label: C
options.text: LDA is a bulky, sterically hindered base; at -78°C (irreversible kinetic control), it abstracts the most sterically accessible proton much faster to form the less substituted enolate.

options.label: D
options.text: LDA coordinates exclusively with the oxygen atom.

questions.correct_answer: LDA is a bulky, sterically hindered base; at -78°C (irreversible kinetic control), it abstracts the most sterically accessible proton much faster to form the less substituted enolate.
questions.explanation: Steric hindrance and low temperature prevent equilibration, trapping the kinetically formed less substituted enolate.

questions.chapter_title: Alpha Carbon Chemistry: Enols and Enolates
questions.question: Under what conditions does 2-methylcyclohexanone convert selectively to the more substituted (thermodynamic) enolate?

options.label: A
options.text: Using LDA at -78°C in anhydrous THF.

options.label: B
options.text: Using zinc metal in hydrochloric acid.

options.label: C
options.text: Using elemental sodium in liquid ammonia.

options.label: D
options.text: Using an unhindered base (e.g., NaOEt or KOtBu at room temperature) in a protic solvent, allowing reversible proton transfers to establish thermodynamic equilibrium.

questions.correct_answer: Using an unhindered base (e.g., NaOEt or KOtBu at room temperature) in a protic solvent, allowing reversible proton transfers to establish thermodynamic equilibrium.
questions.explanation: Reversible deprotonation at ambient temperatures allows the system to equilibrate to the more substituted, more stable tetrasubstituted enolate double bond.

questions.chapter_title: Alpha Carbon Chemistry: Enols and Enolates
questions.question: What is the key bond-forming step in the base-catalyzed self-aldol addition of acetaldehyde?

options.label: A
options.text: Nucleophilic attack of the resonance-stabilized enolate α-carbon on the carbonyl carbon of a second acetaldehyde molecule to forge a new C-C bond.

options.label: B
options.text: Homolytic coupling of two formyl radicals.

options.label: C
options.text: Proton transfer from methyl to methyl.

options.label: D
options.text: Attack of the enolate oxygen on the carbonyl carbon.

questions.correct_answer: Nucleophilic attack of the resonance-stabilized enolate α-carbon on the carbonyl carbon of a second acetaldehyde molecule to forge a new C-C bond.
questions.explanation: Enolates react as carbon nucleophiles (soft center) attacking the electrophilic carbonyl carbon of an aldehyde to create the β-hydroxy aldehyde.

questions.chapter_title: Alpha Carbon Chemistry: Enols and Enolates
questions.question: Why does dehydration of an aldol addition product proceed via an E1cB mechanism rather than E2 or E1?

options.label: A
options.text: The reaction proceeds via a tertiary carbocation.

options.label: B
options.text: The α-hydrogen is acidified by the adjacent carbonyl, allowing base to deprotonate it to an enolate anion, which subsequently expels the poor leaving group (OH⁻) to form a conjugated enone.

options.label: C
options.text: Hydroxide is an excellent leaving group that falls off spontaneously.

options.label: D
options.text: The reaction requires high-energy UV light.

questions.correct_answer: The α-hydrogen is acidified by the adjacent carbonyl, allowing base to deprotonate it to an enolate anion, which subsequently expels the poor leaving group (OH⁻) to form a conjugated enone.
questions.explanation: Acidic α-protons allow formation of a carbanion/enolate intermediate (E1cB) that expels hydroxide driven by extended conjugation in the α,β-unsaturated enone.

questions.chapter_title: Alpha Carbon Chemistry: Enols and Enolates
questions.question: What irreversible elementary step drives the Claisen condensation of ethyl acetate to completion?

options.label: A
options.text: Precipitation of sodium metal.

options.label: B
options.text: Deprotonation of the newly formed β-keto ester (pKa ~ 11) by ethoxide to generate a resonance-stabilized enolate salt, which requires acid workup to yield the neutral product.

options.label: C
options.text: Spontaneous loss of carbon dioxide.

options.label: D
options.text: Evaporation of ethanol from the flask.

questions.correct_answer: Deprotonation of the newly formed β-keto ester (pKa ~ 11) by ethoxide to generate a resonance-stabilized enolate salt, which requires acid workup to yield the neutral product.
questions.explanation: The β-keto ester is ~5 pKa units more acidic than ethanol; its quantitative deprotonation pulls the unfavorable equilibrium forward irreversibly.

questions.chapter_title: Alpha Carbon Chemistry: Enols and Enolates
questions.question: Why does diethyl heptanedioate (diethyl pimelate) undergo Dieckmann cyclization to form a 6-membered ring rather than an 8-membered ring?

options.label: A
options.text: The seven-carbon chain cannot form enolates.

options.label: B
options.text: Eight-membered rings are aromatic.

options.label: C
options.text: Six-membered rings have zero entropy.

options.label: D
options.text: Intramolecular nucleophilic attack of the enolate on the distal ester forms a strain-free six-membered tetrahedral intermediate, which is kinetically and thermodynamically favored.

questions.correct_answer: Intramolecular nucleophilic attack of the enolate on the distal ester forms a strain-free six-membered tetrahedral intermediate, which is kinetically and thermodynamically favored.
questions.explanation: 5- and 6-membered ring formations have low activation barriers and minimal ring strain compared to medium rings (7–9 membered).

questions.chapter_title: Alpha Carbon Chemistry: Enols and Enolates
questions.question: Why do enolates of β-dicarbonyl compounds (e.g., diethyl malonate) add to the β-carbon of α,β-unsaturated ketones (1,4-addition) rather than the carbonyl carbon (1,2-addition)?

options.label: A
options.text: Resonance-delocalized, highly stabilized enolates are 'soft' nucleophiles that match the soft electrophilic character of the β-carbon (HOMO-LUMO orbital control).

options.label: B
options.text: 1,2-Addition produces an antiaromatic product.

options.label: C
options.text: The carbonyl carbon is sterically completely blocked.

options.label: D
options.text: The β-carbon bears a formal full positive charge.

questions.correct_answer: Resonance-delocalized, highly stabilized enolates are 'soft' nucleophiles that match the soft electrophilic character of the β-carbon (HOMO-LUMO orbital control).
questions.explanation: Soft, delocalized nucleophiles react under orbital control at the softer β-carbon of conjugated systems (1,4-conjugate addition).

questions.chapter_title: Alpha Carbon Chemistry: Enols and Enolates
questions.question: What two fundamental named reactions occur sequentially in a Robinson annulation?

options.label: A
options.text: A Wittig reaction followed by a Wolff-Kishner reduction.

options.label: B
options.text: A Friedel-Crafts acylation followed by Clemmensen reduction.

options.label: C
options.text: A Michael 1,4-conjugate addition followed by an intramolecular aldol condensation, constructing a fused six-membered α,β-unsaturated cyclohexenone ring.

options.label: D
options.text: A Diels-Alder reaction followed by a Claisen rearrangement.

questions.correct_answer: A Michael 1,4-conjugate addition followed by an intramolecular aldol condensation, constructing a fused six-membered α,β-unsaturated cyclohexenone ring.
questions.explanation: Robinson annulation combines a Michael conjugate addition with an intramolecular aldol condensation to forge a new cyclohexenone ring.

questions.chapter_title: Alpha Carbon Chemistry: Enols and Enolates
questions.topic: Malonic Ester Decarboxylation Cyclic Transition State
questions.question: What is the mechanism of thermal decarboxylation of a β-dicarboxylic acid in the malonic ester synthesis?

options.label: A
options.text: Direct SN2 displacement of carboxylate by water.

options.label: B
options.text: A concerted six-membered cyclic transition state transfers the acidic proton to the second carbonyl oxygen, expelling CO₂ and forming a transient enol that tautomerizes to carboxylic acid.

options.label: C
options.text: Unimolecular loss of CO gas followed by oxidation.

options.label: D
options.text: Homolytic cleavage of the C-C bond to form CO₂ radical.

questions.correct_answer: A concerted six-membered cyclic transition state transfers the acidic proton to the second carbonyl oxygen, expelling CO₂ and forming a transient enol that tautomerizes to carboxylic acid.
questions.explanation: Thermal decarboxylation of β-keto acids and β-diacids proceeds through a 6-membered cyclic transition state yielding an enol and carbon dioxide.

questions.question: Why do enolates of β-dicarbonyl compounds (e.g., diethyl malonate) add to the β-carbon of α,β-unsaturated ketones (1,4-addition) rather than the carbonyl carbon (1,2-addition)?

options.label: A

options.text: 1,2-Addition produces an antiaromatic product.

options.label: D

questions.question: What two fundamental named reactions occur sequentially in a Robinson annulation?

options.text: A Diels-Alder reaction followed by a Claisen rearrangement.

options.label: C

questions.correct_answer: A Michael 1,4-conjugate addition followed by an intramolecular aldol condensation, constructing a fused six-membered α,β-unsaturated cyclohexenone ring.
questions.explanation: Robinson annulation combines a Michael conjugate addition with an intramolecular aldol condensation to forge a new cyclohexenone ring.

questions.chapter_title: Alpha Carbon Chemistry: Enols and Enolates
questions.topic: Malonic Ester Decarboxylation Cyclic Transition State
questions.question: What is the mechanism of thermal decarboxylation of a β-dicarboxylic acid in the malonic ester synthesis?

options.label: A
options.text: Homolytic cleavage of the C-C bond to form CO₂ radical.

options.label: B
options.text: Unimolecular loss of CO gas followed by oxidation.

options.label: C
options.text: A concerted six-membered cyclic transition state transfers the acidic proton to the second carbonyl oxygen, expelling CO₂ and forming a transient enol that tautomerizes to carboxylic acid.

options.label: D
options.text: Direct SN2 displacement of carboxylate by water.

questions.correct_answer: A concerted six-membered cyclic transition state transfers the acidic proton to the second carbonyl oxygen, expelling CO₂ and forming a transient enol that tautomerizes to carboxylic acid.

questions.chapter_title: Alpha Carbon Chemistry: Enols and Enolates
questions.topic: Keto-Enol Tautomerism Acid vs Base Mechanism
questions.question: What is the difference in intermediate charge state between acid-catalyzed and base-catalyzed keto-enol tautomerism?

options.label: A
options.text: Base catalysis proceeds with retention; acid catalysis with inversion.

options.label: B
options.text: There is no intermediate in either pathway.

options.label: C
options.text: Acid catalysis proceeds via a positively charged oxocarbenium intermediate, whereas base catalysis proceeds via a negatively charged resonance-stabilized enolate intermediate.

options.label: D
options.text: Acid catalysis forms a radical; base catalysis forms an anion.

questions.correct_answer: Acid catalysis proceeds via a positively charged oxocarbenium intermediate, whereas base catalysis proceeds via a negatively charged resonance-stabilized enolate intermediate.
questions.explanation: Acid mechanisms feature protonation first (cationic intermediates); base mechanisms feature deprotonation first (anionic enolate intermediates).

questions.chapter_title: Alpha Carbon Chemistry: Enols and Enolates
questions.question: Why does lithium diisopropylamide (LDA) at -78°C selectively abstract the less hindered α-proton of 2-methylcyclohexanone?

options.label: A
options.text: The less substituted enolate is thermodynamically more stable.

options.label: B
options.text: LDA coordinates exclusively with the oxygen atom.

options.label: C
options.text: LDA is a bulky, sterically hindered base; at -78°C (irreversible kinetic control), it abstracts the most sterically accessible proton much faster to form the less substituted enolate.

options.label: D
options.text: LDA is a weak base that equilibrates to the thermodynamic product.

questions.correct_answer: LDA is a bulky, sterically hindered base; at -78°C (irreversible kinetic control), it abstracts the most sterically accessible proton much faster to form the less substituted enolate.
questions.explanation: Steric hindrance and low temperature prevent equilibration, trapping the kinetically formed less substituted enolate.

questions.chapter_title: Alpha Carbon Chemistry: Enols and Enolates
questions.question: Under what conditions does 2-methylcyclohexanone convert selectively to the more substituted (thermodynamic) enolate?

options.label: A
options.text: Using an unhindered base (e.g., NaOEt or KOtBu at room temperature) in a protic solvent, allowing reversible proton transfers to establish thermodynamic equilibrium.

options.label: B
options.text: Using elemental sodium in liquid ammonia.

options.label: C
options.text: Using zinc metal in hydrochloric acid.

options.label: D
options.text: Using LDA at -78°C in anhydrous THF.

questions.correct_answer: Using an unhindered base (e.g., NaOEt or KOtBu at room temperature) in a protic solvent, allowing reversible proton transfers to establish thermodynamic equilibrium.
questions.explanation: Reversible deprotonation at ambient temperatures allows the system to equilibrate to the more substituted, more stable tetrasubstituted enolate double bond.

questions.chapter_title: Alpha Carbon Chemistry: Enols and Enolates
questions.question: What is the key bond-forming step in the base-catalyzed self-aldol addition of acetaldehyde?

options.label: A
options.text: Proton transfer from methyl to methyl.

options.label: B
options.text: Nucleophilic attack of the resonance-stabilized enolate α-carbon on the carbonyl carbon of a second acetaldehyde molecule to forge a new C-C bond.

options.label: C
options.text: Attack of the enolate oxygen on the carbonyl carbon.

options.label: D
options.text: Homolytic coupling of two formyl radicals.

questions.correct_answer: Nucleophilic attack of the resonance-stabilized enolate α-carbon on the carbonyl carbon of a second acetaldehyde molecule to forge a new C-C bond.
questions.explanation: Enolates react as carbon nucleophiles (soft center) attacking the electrophilic carbonyl carbon of an aldehyde to create the β-hydroxy aldehyde.

questions.chapter_title: Alpha Carbon Chemistry: Enols and Enolates
questions.question: Why does dehydration of an aldol addition product proceed via an E1cB mechanism rather than E2 or E1?

options.label: A
options.text: The reaction requires high-energy UV light.

options.label: B
options.text: The α-hydrogen is acidified by the adjacent carbonyl, allowing base to deprotonate it to an enolate anion, which subsequently expels the poor leaving group (OH⁻) to form a conjugated enone.

options.label: C
options.text: Hydroxide is an excellent leaving group that falls off spontaneously.

options.label: D
options.text: The reaction proceeds via a tertiary carbocation.

questions.correct_answer: The α-hydrogen is acidified by the adjacent carbonyl, allowing base to deprotonate it to an enolate anion, which subsequently expels the poor leaving group (OH⁻) to form a conjugated enone.
questions.explanation: Acidic α-protons allow formation of a carbanion/enolate intermediate (E1cB) that expels hydroxide driven by extended conjugation in the α,β-unsaturated enone.

questions.chapter_title: Alpha Carbon Chemistry: Enols and Enolates
questions.question: What irreversible elementary step drives the Claisen condensation of ethyl acetate to completion?

options.label: A
options.text: Deprotonation of the newly formed β-keto ester (pKa ~ 11) by ethoxide to generate a resonance-stabilized enolate salt, which requires acid workup to yield the neutral product.

options.label: B
options.text: Spontaneous loss of carbon dioxide.

options.label: C
options.text: Precipitation of sodium metal.

options.label: D
options.text: Evaporation of ethanol from the flask.

questions.correct_answer: Deprotonation of the newly formed β-keto ester (pKa ~ 11) by ethoxide to generate a resonance-stabilized enolate salt, which requires acid workup to yield the neutral product.
questions.explanation: The β-keto ester is ~5 pKa units more acidic than ethanol; its quantitative deprotonation pulls the unfavorable equilibrium forward irreversibly.
